source_guidance_span.quote: Organs can be left in CUBIC-R + at room temperature. The maximum storage period depends on the staining dye. Organs stained with PI and RD2 can be stored for >1 month at room temperature in a dark environment. Avoid storage at 4 °C, so that the samples do not crystallize.

source_recipe_span.quote:
6. SeeDB2 solutions
Notes:
a. Tris-EDTA buffer pH 7.6 (Recipe 2) is used to prepare SeeDB2S from Histodenz powder.
Do not use PBS. Phosphate buffer will generate white precipitates after long-term storage
and impair imaging quality.
b. The solution of 0.01% sodium azide can be included in the buffer for long-term preservation.
Do not store clearing solution for long time.
c. Pre-made SeeDB2 solutions are also commercialized from FUJIFILM Wako Pure Chemical.
Solutions Composition
SeeDB2G with saponin
(clearing)
2% saponin in Omnipaque350
SeeDB2G (mounting) Use Omnipaque350 directly
Or 7,500 μl Tris-EDTA (pH 7.6) + 10 g Histodenz
SeeDB2S with saponin
(clearing)
3,780 μl Tris-EDTA (pH 7.6) + 420 μl 20% saponin sol ution + 10 g
Histodenz
SeeDB2S (mounting) 4,200 μl Tris-EDTA (pH 7.6) + 10 g Histodenz
Add 4,200 μl Tris-EDTA to a 50 ml conical tube, and then add 10 g
Histodenz. Use a rotator to fully dissolve the Histodenz in the conical
tube

source_guidance_span.quote:
After official publication of our protocol in bio -protocol ( https://bio-protocol.org/e3046), we noted an error in the
protocol.
The recipe for Phosphate -buffered saline (PBS) was in fact the one for 10x PBS. Accordingly, we need to make
corrections as follows (in Recipes):
“1. Phosphate-buffered saline (PBS)” → “1. 10x Phosphate-buffered saline (10x PBS)”.
“Add ddH2O to prepare 1 L PBS” → “Add ddH2O to prepare 1 L 10x PBS. Dilute 10 times with ddH 2O to prepare 1x
PBS”.

rules.source_procedure_scope: Recipe 6a: SeeDB2S from Histodenz powder; complete Recipe 6 on PAGE12
rules.source_scope_limit: Powder PBS preparation is author-recipe nonconformance; stock PBS dilution is local potential risk. Unquantified long-term storage does not prove current precipitation or failure. G and PBS tissue washes are excluded.
